role: calibration only (solution-geometry fingerprint: lex-first ≠ max-z, A257843)
missing_theorem: Explanation (derived here, elementary): for p ≡ 5 (mod 8), p > 5, the lex-first solution x₀ = (p+3)/4 (e = 3), y₀ = (px₀ + 2)/3, z₀ = px₀y₀/2 is also the max-z solution. Reason: px₀ ≡ p² ≡ 1 (mod 3), so δ = 3y − px₀ = 2 is the least defect, and z₀ is integral because x₀ is even, giving z₀ ≈ p⁴/96. Every e ≥ 7 gives z ≤ px(px+1)/e ≲ p⁴/112. For p ≡ 1 (8), x₀ is odd, pxy is odd, so δ = 2 fails at e = 3, and an e ≥ 7 slice with δ = 1 can win. Hence membership is confined to p ≡ 1 (mod 8), as Pass 1 observed.
status_ref: this pass (argument in missing_theorem; scripts/z52d_avenue_Q12_lexmaxz.py confirms max-z = (x₀, y₀, z₀) at all 109 primes ≡ 5 (8), 13 ≤ p < 3000); Pass 1 U05 (0 of ~570 primes ≡ 5 (8) are members; 25 % of 1 (24), 67 % of 17 (24))
